title: Quail Hub retail edge integration jot
body:
Context / why this exists:
Quick scratchpad from initial Quail Hub (regional retail chain) kickoff — they want Redwood Private running in their regional edge racks to power in-store assistants (product lookup, returns, store staff prompts). This doc captures call notes, technical constraints, known gotchas, immediate next steps and owners. Intended to be informal — will turn into a formal onboarding runbook once we lock network/KMS details.

Summary from 2024-09-18 kickoff (60m):
- Attendees: Aisha (SE), Rafael (Solutions Eng), Maya (Customer Success), Theo (Quail Hub infra lead), Priyanka (Quail Hub security), Liam (Store ops).
- High-level ask: private deploy inside Quail Hub’s 3 regional peering locations (NE, MW, SW). Each location: 2x DGX-ish racks (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), intermittent WAN (store-to-edge) connectivity. SLA: sub-100ms median token latency for short chat flows (<=128 tokens), 99.5% uptime.
- Data requirement: PII from loyalty program will be used in prompts but must not leave region. They require KMS integration and audit logs.

Key technical constraints / notes observed on call:
1) Network topology and egress:
   - Edge racks currently NAT behind a single egress IP block per region (managed by Quail NetOps). They will not allow outbound to internet except via corporate proxy. Means Redwood Private control plane must either be reachable via proxy (supported) or operate via an in-region control plane instance.
   - Stores connect to edge racks over a mix of MPLS and IPsec; packet loss and jitter reported during peak night restocks. Need to validate RPC timeouts and backpressure behavior on lossy links.

2) Model placement, size, and quantization:
   - Their initial target model: small-medium chat model for staff prompts (about 7B FP16 equivalent). Preference for a quantized 8-bit or 4-bit optimized binary to save memory and increase concurrency.
   - Want a fallback to hosted Redwood models for large generative tasks during maintenance windows. Need explicit policy for automatic fallbacks (policy should respect data locality — e.g., scrub/omit PII before fallback).

3) KV/prefix caching and cold start behavior:
   - Many assistant flows will use short contextual histories (32-64 tokens) + store context (static inventory snippets). We should prototype prefix caching on the edge nodes — but need to confirm persistence across restarts.

4) KMS/HSM and keys:
   - Quail Hub prefers AWS KMS with customer-managed keys (CMKs) in each region. They also asked about HSM for highest-tier stores. Confirm whether Redwood Private supports multiple KMS endpoints and per-region key rotation policies.

5) Compliance and logging:
   - Audit trail must show model version, prompt hash (not full prompt when PII present), request origin (store id) and SLO met/miss indicators. We should offer a log redaction option in the agent that strips sensitive fields before export.

6) Observability hooks and cost reporting:
   - They want cost attribution per-store and per-feature (returns assistant vs. general search). Need to map token-level accounting to store ids; confirm how Redwood Console can surface this for private deployments (agent-level tags, route-level costing).

7) Ops and deploy cadence:
   - Quail Hub ops run maintenance windows Tuesdays 01:00-04:00 local. They asked about safe automatic upgrades and quick rollback. Recommend canary on 10% of stores in a region for two weeks before region-wide rollout.

Immediate gotchas / risks called out (to keep visible):
- Control plane reachability: proxy-only environments will require extra config; if not solved early, stalls onboarding.
- Token leakage via fallback: default fallback to hosted API may cause PII leakage; must ensure prompt scrubbing pipeline is plumbed for any fallback path.
- Unreliable store-to-edge links may inflate latencies; need to test behavior with simulated packet loss.
- Inventory freshness expectations: store managers expect <30s update after sync — may be unrealistic for full reindex. Need to set expectations and design a delta-sync approach.

Notes from demos/requests during call:
- Theo: wants a small demo that runs model locally in their staging rack behind the proxy by Oct 1. He asked for a scripted deploy (Terraform + Helm) to be handed off.
- Priyanka: wants to see exact audit log fields before sign-off.
- Liam: cares about store-level UI latency and wants a comparison table of 7B quantized vs hosted 13B in terms of median latency and cost per 1000 requests.

Open questions (to resolve ASAP):
- Q1: Can we support control plane comms via corporate HTTP proxy? (Action: Rafael to validate with infra team and document proxy config by 2024-09-25).
- Q2: Does Redwood Private support per-region CMKs with auto-rotate? (Action: Aisha + Maya to confirm with platform by 2024-09-22).
- Q3: What scrub rules are acceptable for loyalty PII before fallback? (Action: Priyanka to provide sample PII patterns and compliance rules by 2024-09-27).
- Q4: Can we produce token-level cost by store id in Console for private deployments (route tagging)? (Action: Theo + Rafael to map store→route patterns and send sample logs by 2024-09-24).

Proposed short-term plan (next 4 weeks):
1) Prep staging deploy script + quickstart: provide Terraform/Helm repo template; include sample proxy env var config and KMS placeholders. Owner: Rafael. ETA: 2024-10-01.
2) Small perf bake: run quantized 7B binary on a 1-rack staging node and capture median latencies across 128-token chat flows with simulated 1%/5% packet loss. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2024-10-07.
3) Privacy/fallback doc: sketch scrub rules and abort/fallback flow. Owner: Maya with Priyanka. ETA: 2024-09-27.
4) Observability mapping: propose Console view mock-ups showing per-store cost and latency. Owner: Solutions UX (Rafael + Maya). ETA: 2024-10-04.

Longer-term notes (for the onboarding runbook):
- Consider enabling persistent KV cache with on-disk snapshot to reduce cold-start penalty between restarts. Validate write durability requirements for store inventory.
- Model scaling: plan for cross-region model replication if a region experiences hardware fault — route traffic to nearest region while preserving PII egress rules.
- Autoscaling: configure instance pools with conservative burst capacity; ensure policy doesn't spin up new nodes during degraded network conditions triggering more flakiness.

Action items (owner + due):
- Rafael: write staging Terraform/Helm template + checklist (2024-10-01).
- Aisha: perf runs + packet-loss sim (2024-10-07).
- Maya: draft privacy scrub doc + fallback rules (2024-09-27).
- Priyanka (Quail): sample PII patterns + compliance checklist (2024-09-27).
- Theo (Quail): provide sample network diagrams and store→edge routing table (2024-09-24).

Random small things to remember in follow-ups:
- Ask about store hardware GPU drivers; some racks still on 470.xx drivers which break recent CUDA kernels.
- Confirm timezone for region scheduling (they use local times, not UTC).
- Provide a short slide deck targeted at VP Ops summarizing SLOs and expected cost delta (hosted vs private) to help get budget approval.

End notes: keep this doc informal. Will migrate finalized runbook + security checklist to confluence once Q1-Q3 resolved.

Snippet: suggested stub README (to include in template repo):
- README.md: quickstart -> prerequisites (proxy creds, CMK ARN, store routing map) -> terraform init -> helm deploy --set controlPlane.proxy=true --set kms.arn=arn:aws:kms:...

-- Aisha
